title: Bipolar Nebula Outters 4
caption: The bipolar nebula Outters 4 within Sh2-129, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: A blue, two-lobed nebula is embedded in a vast red glow in this image in Cepheus. The blue structure is Outters 4, a bipolar nebula, and the red is Sh2-129, a giant HII emission nebula.

A bipolar nebula has two lobes extending in opposite directions, often shaped by outflows of gas. An HII region is a cloud of hydrogen whose atoms have been stripped of electrons by strong starlight, making it glow.

Outters 4 is named after Nicolas Outters, the amateur astronomer who discovered it. Its origin remains uncertain, and it is not yet clear whether it is linked to HR 8119, the bright star at the center of the image. Answering that question would help astronomers explain what created the lobes.

understand.summary: The Mayall 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic camera used two narrowband filters. Hydrogen-alpha is shown in red and sulfur [S II] in blue.
filters: 672 nm · Optical Sll (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
656 nm · Optical Ha (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
